title: The Universal Testimony Of The Cosmos 18th Degree 2nd Truth Mutual Assistance

questions.question: What main change in the world is described as happening every fall and every spring?
questions.answer: In fall, a world of living things passes away, and in spring, a new world of living things appears.

questions.question: How are these changes said to happen?
questions.answer: They happen in a highly ordered, regular, and balanced way.

questions.question: What comparison is used for the world because living beings come, stay for a while, and then leave?
questions.answer: It is compared to a temporary stopping place for travelers.

questions.question: In that comparison, what do the living worlds do before they leave?
questions.answer: They carry out their assigned purposes and then move on.

questions.question: What does this repeated order in death and new life point to about the Creator?
questions.answer: It points to His necessary existence, limitless power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What kinds of things does the passage say the Creator brings into existence in this world?
questions.answer: He brings into being living realms and meaningful, purposeful worlds.

questions.question: With what qualities are these brought into existence?
questions.answer: They are brought with wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: For what kinds of purposes are these created things then used?
questions.answer: They are used for lordly purposes, Divine aims, and merciful goals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about contingence in relation to the universe?
questions.answer: It says contingence covers and surrounds the whole universe.

questions.question: Which range of things is included when the passage speaks about all beings?
questions.answer: It includes everything from the highest created levels to the earth, and from the tiniest particles to huge heavenly bodies.

questions.question: What are some of the special features each thing receives?
questions.answer: Each thing is given its own essence, form, identity, qualities, and useful parts.

questions.question: Why is giving one exact form to a thing important in the argument?
questions.answer: Because many forms were possible, so choosing one fitting form shows deliberate choice.

questions.question: Why does the giving of a distinct identity matter?
questions.answer: Because a being could have been like many others, but it is singled out in a precise and suitable way.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the attributes and organs given to created things?
questions.answer: They are especially suited, useful, and wise, not random or pointless.

questions.question: What do all these choices among many possibilities prove?
questions.answer: They prove the necessary existence, infinite power, and unlimited wisdom of the One who chooses and creates.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s knowledge of things?
questions.answer: Nothing is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What does it teach about difficulty for Allah in creation?
questions.answer: Nothing is hard for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating a spring, a tree, and a seed?
questions.answer: It says creating a spring is as easy for Him as creating a tree, and creating a tree is as easy as creating a seed.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the testimony of the universe?
questions.answer: It is described as a great testimony with two wings.

questions.question: In this passage, which wing is being explained?
questions.answer: The wing connected to contingence is being explained here.

questions.question: What yearly pattern in nature is highlighted at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: A vast dying in autumn and a fresh coming-to-life in spring.

questions.question: Why is that yearly pattern important in the passage?
questions.answer: It is used as evidence that creation is controlled with wisdom and purpose.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of deaths and new creations within these seasons?
questions.answer: It says there are many separate ones, all happening in an organized way.

questions.question: What picture helps explain the temporary stay of living beings in the world?
questions.answer: The world is pictured like an inn or resting place for travelers.

questions.question: What does that picture suggest about this worldly life?
questions.answer: It suggests that life here is temporary and that beings come and go according to a plan.

questions.question: What can clear-minded people understand from this order?
questions.answer: They can understand that there is a glorious Creator with necessary existence, perfect power, and wisdom.

questions.question: Which qualities of the Creator are especially connected to bringing worlds into being?
questions.answer: Power, wisdom, knowledge, balance, and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying those worlds are used for Divine aims?
questions.answer: Their existence and activities serve meanings and purposes set by Allah.

questions.question: What does “contingence” mean in this passage in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means created things could have been otherwise, so they depend on a chooser and creator.

questions.question: Does the passage limit contingence to only small things? Explain.
questions.answer: No. It includes both the largest and the smallest things, and both general and individual beings.

questions.question: What are two examples of specific features each being receives?
questions.answer: It receives a particular shape and a distinct identity.

questions.question: Why does choosing one essence from many possibilities point beyond the thing itself?
questions.answer: Because the thing could not choose itself from endless options, so a chooser must have specified it.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a creature before it is given fitting qualities and organs?
questions.answer: It is described as lacking direction among many possibilities.

questions.question: What does giving beneficial organs show about creation?
questions.answer: It shows careful planning, usefulness, and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do these acts of specifying and distinguishing show about the Creator’s power?
questions.answer: They show that His power is unlimited.

questions.question: According to the passage, what do they show about the Creator’s wisdom?
questions.answer: They show that His wisdom reaches everything in a precise way.

questions.question: What statement in the passage shows Allah’s full awareness of creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that no thing and no matter is concealed from Him.

questions.question: What comparison teaches that great and small creations are equally easy for Allah?
questions.answer: The comparison between a whole spring, a tree, and a seed.

questions.question: What role does contingence play in the universe’s testimony?
questions.answer: It forms one wing of the universe’s great witness to Allah.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The order, choice, and precision in creation point to Allah’s necessary existence, power, wisdom, and mercy.

questions.question: What two seasons are used to show repeated change in the world?
questions.answer: Autumn and spring.

questions.question: What happens to the world in autumn according to the passage?
questions.answer: A great living world passes away.

questions.question: What happens in spring?
questions.answer: A fresh living world is brought forth.

questions.question: Is this change described as chaotic or arranged?
questions.answer: It is described as arranged with order and regularity.

questions.question: Why does the passage compare the world to a place where travelers stop briefly?
questions.answer: Because beings stay only for a limited time, complete their tasks, and then depart.

questions.question: What does the regular coming and going of living worlds show about the One managing them?
questions.answer: It shows He has necessary existence and possesses endless power and wisdom.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that creation is not pointless?
questions.answer: It says these worlds are brought forth for meaningful purposes and merciful goals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the spread of contingence in the universe?
questions.answer: It says contingence is found everywhere throughout it.

questions.question: Which kinds of things are included in that claim?
questions.answer: Everything, whether universal or particular, large or small.

questions.question: What does every created thing receive besides existence itself?
questions.answer: It receives a certain nature, a fitting shape, a unique identity, and useful qualities and parts.

questions.question: Why is the idea of “many possibilities” repeated so often?
questions.answer: To show that the exact outcome was chosen deliberately, not by chance.

questions.question: If a thing could have taken many forms, what does its single exact form point to?
questions.answer: It points to a wise chooser who selected that exact form.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the assignment of attributes to a creature?
questions.answer: As giving it special and suitable traits that benefit it.

questions.question: What does the giving of useful organs add to the argument?
questions.answer: It shows not just choice, but wise and purposeful choice.

questions.question: What three major truths are supported by all these examples of specification?
questions.answer: Allah’s necessary existence, His infinite power, and His unlimited wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s relation to hidden things?
questions.answer: Nothing at all is hidden from Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability to handle large and small acts of creation?
questions.answer: The largest and smallest are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Which example shows that creating something huge is easy for Allah?
questions.answer: Bringing forth a whole spring.

questions.question: Which example shows that creating something tiny is also easy for Allah?
questions.answer: Bringing forth a seed.

questions.question: In the image of the cosmos giving witness, what is contingence compared to?
questions.answer: It is compared to one wing of that witness.

questions.question: What broad event happens to the world every autumn in the passage?
questions.answer: A vast realm of living things comes to an end.

questions.question: What broad event happens every spring?
questions.answer: A new realm of life is created.

questions.question: What is important about the way these events happen?
questions.answer: They happen with exact order and steady regularity.

questions.question: What metaphor is used to explain the world’s temporary nature?
questions.answer: The world is described like a lodging place for travelers.

questions.question: In that metaphor, what are living beings like?
questions.answer: They are like travelers who stay briefly, do their work, and continue on.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from this orderly pattern?
questions.answer: There must be a glorious Creator with necessary existence, boundless power, and endless wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Creator’s way of making these living worlds?
questions.answer: He makes them with perfect wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: Why are these worlds said to exist?
questions.answer: They exist to serve Divine and merciful purposes.

questions.question: What does the passage claim about contingence and the whole cosmos?
questions.answer: It claims that contingence surrounds the entire cosmos.

questions.question: What scale of creation does the passage mention to show this?
questions.answer: It mentions everything from the highest created realm down to the earth, and from atoms to planets.

questions.question: Name three things each being is said to receive.
questions.answer: It receives a particular essence, a certain form, and a distinct identity.

questions.question: How does the passage show that these features are not random?
questions.answer: It says each one is selected from countless possible options.

questions.question: What does selecting one identity from many possible members of a kind show?
questions.answer: It shows exact distinction and deliberate choice.

questions.question: How are the qualities and organs of creatures described?
questions.answer: They are described as wise, suitable, and beneficial.

questions.question: What do these careful choices testify to?
questions.answer: They testify to the necessary existence, infinite power, and unlimited wisdom of the Creator.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s awareness of every object and matter?
questions.answer: Every object and matter is fully known to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about difficulty in Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: No task is difficult for Him.

questions.question: What comparison is given to help us understand this ease?
questions.answer: Producing an entire spring is as easy for Him as producing a tree, and a tree as easy as a seed.

questions.question: What is the relationship between contingence and the cosmos’s testimony?
questions.answer: Contingence is one part, or one wing, of that testimony.

questions.question: What central belief is the passage strengthening through these examples?
questions.answer: Belief that Allah alone creates and governs everything with power and wisdom.

questions.question: What repeated life cycle of the world is described in the passage?
questions.answer: A great dying in autumn followed by a great renewal in spring.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the order of these repeated events?
questions.answer: It says they happen with careful arrangement and regular pattern.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a stop on a journey?
questions.answer: Because living beings are here only for a time before moving on.

questions.question: What do these passing worlds do during their stay?
questions.answer: They fulfill the duties assigned to them.

questions.question: What does such organized change reveal to the mind?
questions.answer: It reveals a Creator whose existence is necessary and whose power and wisdom are unlimited.

questions.question: What kinds of created realities are said to be brought into existence?
questions.answer: Living domains and meaningful universes.

questions.question: Which qualities show that these are made with care?
questions.answer: They are made with wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: What final use is mentioned for these created worlds?
questions.answer: They are employed for Divine, lordly, and merciful purposes.

questions.question: What is the main point of the section about contingence?
questions.answer: Created things depend on a chooser because they could have been many other ways.

questions.question: Is contingence described as affecting only one part of creation or all of it?
questions.answer: All of it.

questions.question: What examples are given to show the full range of created things?
questions.answer: From the highest realm to the ground, and from atoms to planets.

questions.question: What individual features are given to each thing?
questions.answer: A special nature, a fitting appearance, a unique identity, suitable traits, and useful organs.

questions.question: Why does the passage keep mentioning “possibilities” and “probabilities”?
questions.answer: To show that the final form of each creature was selected from many alternatives.

questions.question: What does this selection teach us about the Creator?
questions.answer: He chooses with knowledge and creates with wisdom and power.

questions.question: How does the passage describe creatures before they are given their exact path and equipment?
questions.answer: As standing among many possible ways without direction on their own.

questions.question: What does the fitting arrangement of qualities and organs prove besides power?
questions.answer: It also proves wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about hidden things in relation to Allah?
questions.answer: None of them are hidden from Him.

questions.question: How does the passage explain the ease of all creation for Allah?
questions.answer: It says the biggest act and the smallest act are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Which examples are used to show this equal ease?
questions.answer: Spring, a tree, and a seed.

questions.question: What image sums up the universe’s witness to Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: The universe is giving a great testimony, and contingence is one of its two wings.

questions.question: Which two seasons are used to show the world’s repeated changes?
questions.answer: Fall and spring.

questions.question: What happens on a large scale in fall?
questions.answer: A broad living world comes to an end.

questions.question: What happens on a large scale in spring?
questions.answer: A new living world is brought into existence.

questions.question: How are these large changes described in terms of order?
questions.answer: They are described as orderly, regular, and balanced.

questions.question: What everyday image is used for the world in this part of the text?
questions.answer: A place where travelers stay for a short time.

questions.question: What does that image help us understand about creation?
questions.answer: That beings are temporary guests with duties and a planned departure.

questions.question: From this constant order, what three things become clear about the Creator?
questions.answer: His necessary existence, infinite power, and unending wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say He creates in this world?
questions.answer: He creates living realms and purposeful worlds.

questions.question: Which qualities are named to describe His creating?
questions.answer: Wisdom, knowledge, balance, order, and regularity.

questions.question: What does the passage say these created worlds are used for after being made?
questions.answer: They are used for Divine purposes and merciful goals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how widespread contingence is?
questions.answer: It is found throughout the whole cosmos.

questions.question: Which opposites are listed to show this wide scope?
questions.answer: Universal and particular, big and small.

questions.question: What does every being receive that makes it distinct from others?
questions.answer: Its own essence, form, identity, qualities, and beneficial organs.

questions.question: Why is one exact form out of many possible forms important?
questions.answer: Because it shows that a knowing will selected that exact form.

questions.question: Why is one exact identity out of many possible identities important?
questions.answer: Because it shows the being was distinguished intentionally, not by accident.

questions.question: What do suitable attributes and useful organs tell us about creation?
questions.answer: They show that creation is wise, purposeful, and beneficial.

questions.question: What overall truth do these many acts of selecting and fitting confirm?
questions.answer: They confirm the Creator’s necessary existence and His perfect power and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about whether anything can be concealed from Allah?
questions.answer: Nothing can be concealed from Him.

questions.question: What does it say about the relation between great tasks and small tasks for Allah?
questions.answer: They are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage illustrate that equal ease?
questions.answer: By saying that creating a whole spring is as easy as creating a tree, and a tree as easy as creating a seed.

questions.question: How is contingence connected to the universe’s witness?
questions.answer: It makes up one wing of the universe’s great testimony to Allah.
